critique: The yellow-orange palette is closer and the early frame has a slightly brighter center, but both times still read as a tiny cluster of soft, overlapping round particles. The burst has almost no readable rightward flame/spray silhouette or evolution between 0.01 and 0.08 seconds. It remains much too small, cloudy, and circular for an Explosive muzzle flash, which needs a hard bright ignition core and an elongated directional discharge.

suggestions.why: Make this a short, sparse ignition burst rather than enough simultaneous particles to merge into a uniform puff.
Keep the initial burst visible long enough to resolve into a traveling spray by the 0.08-second render instead of continually replacing it with a similar rounded cluster.
Push the burst outward fast enough to create a visibly directional, separated explosive shape.
Increase the visible scale of the flash so it reads as a muzzle event rather than a small central blob.
Remove the heavy soft edge so individual ignition particles form a sharper flame-like core and spray.
